findings.summary: The Deck arrived pre-drained: 18 decisions were already answered before this session began (timestamps 4m–40m before first load), every undo window already closed. The queue never held more than 3 items, so the batch-review offer that appears at ten-or-more waiting could never be triggered or tested, and 'several decisions' were reduced to two regenerated verification-resolution cards.

No design-approval card and no stale-brief card ever appeared in the Deck — not in the waiting queue and not anywhere in the fully-read answered history — even though the Deck's own empty state promises 'a design to approve, a brief that went stale' will appear there. The landing-page design review exists only as a 'Review and approve landing page design' task on the board, reachable only by navigating away from the Deck.

The two 'verification attempts exhausted' decisions loop: the same two tasks (hero section, competitor pricing) had each been resolved three times before my session and respawned again minutes later, with answer history reading 'Re-run once with a human reviewer — ("final" attempt #4)'. A user who clears the Deck watches it refill with the same two questions.

Waiting-count displays disagree: at one point the Deck header read '2 waiting' while the list below it showed 3 actionable items (2 decisions + 1 spot-check), and moments earlier header and nav badge both said 3 for identical contents. Separately, immediately after a reload the page fully rendered 'Nothing is waiting on you' while one card was actually waiting, correcting itself on the next poll.

Cards can change under the pointer: while I was clicking 'Looks right' on the front card, two new decisions arrived and took over the front of the deck, so the click timed out against a target that had been displaced. On a live queue this makes misclicks on the wrong card plausible.

Batch machinery does exist below the advertised threshold: List view offers 'Select all pending' and a '2 selected — Answer / Dismiss / Defer 7d' action bar, but with only 2 pending decisions the contract's 'select at least five' could not be exercised and no ten-or-more offer was ever shown.
